title: external-ca-support-and-rollback-helper-for-airgap-bootstrap
author: Maya Fernandez
description:
Problem: Customers deploying Redwood Private into air-gapped/on-prem environments often must inject a customer-signed CA bundle into node OS trust stores, ingress certificates, and the local OCI registry. Previous installer iterations required manual, error-prone steps and had limited rollback semantics when an incorrect CA bundle caused control-plane components to fail.

This PR implements: 1) Installer-level external CA handling: the installer can now accept a user-provided CA bundle (PEM) as part of the airgap bundle manifest or via the terraform module. The CA is staged into the sealed bundle and validated during preflight (format, chain completeness, and expiration checks). 2) Bootstrapping helpers: the bootstrap phase installs the CA into the host trust store deterministically (supports deb/rpm and a '/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/' path), and mounts the CA into Helm chart values (controller, loadbalancer ingress, registry-proxy) so TLS handshakes succeed without manual intervention. 3) Safe apply & rollback helper: if post-apply health checks fail due to certificate trust issues, the installer will automatically revert the trust changes and restore previous certificates/state using an atomic rollback that leverages a signed state snapshot stored in the local sealed-bundle directory. 4) Terraform module surface: new variables (external_ca_pem, ca_validate_level) allow infra teams to feed a CA in CI or from vault; outputs include ca_fingerprint and ca_install_manifest for auditing. 5) Kube distro compatibility: added distro-specific install scripts for RHEL8/AlmaLinux, Rocky, Ubuntu 22.04, and Flatcar; each script accounts for the distro's recommended CA paths and update commands. 6) Helm chart updates: charts now accept an extraVolumes/extraVolumeMounts pattern for the CA and a values flag 'trustedCAs.enabled' to toggle automatic injection. 7) Tests & docs: integration tests simulate an OCI registry signed with a test CA and a smoke test that intentionally injects a malformed CA to validate rollback. Documentation includes end-to-end setup, terraform snippets, and troubleshooting steps for common certificate errors.

Why this is safe: Validation gates run during preflight (format, signature, chain check) and in the apply step we do a staged rollout: mount CA in a non-critical pod, run smoke probes, then promote to control plane components. The rollback uses the signed snapshot and is idempotent. The change is backward compatible for deployments that don't set external_ca_pem.

Notes on implementation details: - Preflight validator added under cmd/installer/preflight/ca_validator.go (PEM parsing, chain verification against system trust). - Bootstrap helper scripts: scripts/bootstrap/{debian,redhat,flatcar}_install_ca.sh with idempotent install/uninstall functions. - Helm values and templates modified: charts/redwood-core/templates/_ca.tpl and values.yaml additions. - Terraform: modules/airgap/main.tf accepts external_ca_pem as string, writes a local file during plan/apply only when provided. - State snapshot: installer/state/snapshots stores signed JSON blobs containing component versions and a hash of modified paths. Signatures use the installer's ephemeral keypair; snapshot signing verifies before rollback. - CI: new integration job airgap-ca-tests runs in the benchmark-lab infra and uses a mocked registry with local TLS endpoint.

This PR contains tests and a migration guide; see release notes for operator-level actions.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2025-01-23): Please narrow the scope of the distro scripts; prefer using a small common library to avoid duplication. Also add a defensive timeout around trust store updates so upgrades don't hang.
Maya Fernandez (2025-01-24): Responded: refactored the helper functions to scripts/bootstrap/common_install.sh and added a --timeout flag to the install helper; updated tests to cover timeout path.
Priya Nair (2025-01-27): Security review: ensure the external_ca_pem is never stored in plaintext in CI logs. Suggest redaction at terraform output and scrub in the installer logs.

Maya Fernandez (2025-01-28): Addressed: terraform module now writes the CA to a temporary file with strict permissions and the apply output does not print the PEM; installer logs redact PEM content. Added unit test verifying log redaction.
Ethan Zhao (2025-01-30): Approve after nit: can we add a simple e2e step that simulates an expired CA and demonstrates rollback?
Maya Fernandez (2025-02-01): Added e2e test case expired-ca-rollback in test/integration/airgap and recorded CI run artifacts.
release_notes: Added support for providing an external CA bundle for air-gapped/private installs. Installer will validate, stage, and (optionally) inject the CA into OS trust stores, Helm charts, and registry proxies. New Terraform variables: external_ca_pem, ca_validate_level. Added safe rollback behavior when CA-related failures occur. Docs and migration guide included.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash; release branch inclusion TBD by release manager
additional_context: This PR was motivated by a recent enterprise support case (SUP-4128) where a customer-provided CA caused ingress controller failures during an upgrade. The signed snapshot rollback pattern is reusable for future config-injection workflows and will be proposed as a small library for other installers.
